identity.name: Choro
identity.scope: Brazilian Choro as represented by the cited published corpus and historical studies; not a claim to cover every regional, historical, performance, or contemporary variant.

promotion_blockers: rights-clear analysis plan or separate permission
runtime implementation and deterministic behavior evidence
neighboring-style distinctness comparison before any authenticity claim
substantive preregistered plan with concrete hypotheses/null models and exact plan-to-authorized-source binding

sources.citation: Moss, Fabian C.; Souza, Willian Fernandes; Rohrmeier, Martin. Harmony and form in Brazilian Choro: A corpus-driven approach to musical style analysis. Journal of New Music Research 49(5), 416–437 (2020).
supports: The study transcribed chord symbols and formal structure for 295 representative pieces from the Choro Songbook.
The study reports differences in harmonic relations/chord transitions and key transitions within pieces.
The study reports that harmonies in regular 16- and 32-bar phrases conform to their hypermetrical structure.
The study reports a historical relationship in which older compositions use chords with fewer modifications than younger compositions.
does_not_establish: That every Choro piece has a 16- or 32-bar phrase.
A generator architecture, style route, audible fidelity, or community-recognized authenticity.
A model-ready set of universal numerical thresholds.

reported_study_scope.concentration_note: The paper reports these two composers together account for more than one fifth of the pieces.

sources.source_limit: The dataset is based on published songbook material and does not represent the full diversity of the living tradition.

sources.citation: Mário Sève, O fraseado do Choro: algumas considerações rítmicas e melódicas (published 2014 proceedings; page dated 2015).
supports: A historical discussion of phrase style in Rio de Janeiro from the second half of the nineteenth century to the first half of the twentieth.
Examples discuss polca-lundu, tango brasileiro, choro-amaxixado and choro-sambado contexts.
The article discusses Choro ensembles involving cavaquinho, violão and percussion.
does_not_establish: That any single rhythmic pattern, instrumentation, or subtype is universal to all Choro.
That the chord/form corpus alone is sufficient to test melody, rhythmic feel, or performance practice.

sources.citation: Choro Songbook Corpus, version 1.1, Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.3881347.
supports: The versioned record identifies the archived Choro Songbook Corpus release and links to the DCMLab repository.
does_not_establish: The Rights field says 'Other (Open)' without a further description; that metadata is not itself a specific commercial license.
The paper's data availability statement says non-commercial use, and the related GitHub repository has a separate CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 LICENSE. Resolve the relevant rights before use.

license_and_data_handling.data_handling_decision: Do not copy, commit, bundle, fine-tune on, or use the corpus data in commercial training or a commercial product unless a competent legal review establishes an applicable permission or separately negotiated rights.
permitted_work_now: Cite the publication and repository metadata.
Use the documented field schema to design an analysis plan.
Develop synthetic fixtures whose values are authored independently and do not reproduce corpus excerpts.
before_empirical_analysis: Review license scope and any third-party rights in the transcribed songbook material.
Obtain written permission or select an independently rights-cleared corpus if the intended use is commercial or licensing is uncertain.
Record corpus commit, license text version, exact purpose, allowed outputs and retention/deletion policy.
Do not export substantial derived data or note sequences until permitted use has been reviewed.
license_and_data_handling.published_paper_data_availability: The paper states the dataset is available for non-commercial use; the Zenodo label alone does not define broader permission.
license_and_data_handling.rights_interpretation: Do not infer a commercial-use license from Zenodo's generic 'Other (Open)' metadata. The associated repository separately states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Resolve use-specific rights and underlying Songbook transcription rights before empirical work.

hypotheses.statement: Within the subset of works annotated as regular 16- or 32-bar phrases, harmonic events exhibit phrase-position structure associated with the reported hypermetrical organization.
hypotheses.operationalization: After rights clearance, define the eligible regular-phrase subset before inspecting outcomes; map chord changes to normalized phrase positions; state the tested hypermetrical boundary positions from a source-backed analysis plan; compare observed boundary concentration/position dependence against a within-piece null that preserves event counts and phrase lengths while disrupting phrase-position alignment.
hypotheses.null_model: Pre-registered within-piece circular shift or constrained permutation; document edge handling and the unit of resampling. The exact choice must be fixed before running the candidate dataset.
hypotheses.falsification_or_no_pass: No stable effect under the registered null, effect direction reversed, effect confined to a small unreported subgroup, or insufficient annotated regular phrases. Such an outcome blocks a Choro-specific grammar claim for this feature.
hypotheses.limitations: The source reports a corpus-level pattern, not a universal rule. Do not hard-code 16/32 bars as required for every piece.
hypotheses.pass_threshold: Not set here; pre-register an effect size and uncertainty criterion before licensed evaluation.

hypotheses.statement: Chord transitions and within-piece key transitions carry form/context-conditioned structure that cannot be explained by the corpus's aggregate chord-frequency distribution alone.
hypotheses.operationalization: Estimate transition distributions at the piece/part level, report coverage and sparsity, then compare against a pre-registered shuffle that preserves per-piece chord counts and relevant form strata while disrupting adjacent transition order. Evaluate generalization with pieces held out by composition, not rows randomly split from the same piece.
hypotheses.null_model: Per-piece constrained permutation of chord order within comparable part/form strata; report sensitivity to sparse strata and missing key annotation.
hypotheses.falsification_or_no_pass: The proposed transition features do not outperform the constrained null on held-out pieces, or results vanish under reasonable annotation/stratum choices.
hypotheses.limitations: This would establish corpus-relative structure, not by itself distinguish Choro from Samba, Polka, Maxixe, or other neighboring practices.
hypotheses.pass_threshold: Set only after a pilot power/coverage audit and pre-registration; no numeric threshold is inferred from the abstract.

hypotheses.statement: Among compositions with usable year metadata, measured chord-modification frequency differs with composition period in the direction reported by the study: older pieces have fewer chord modifications on average.
hypotheses.operationalization: Define chord modification from the corpus schema in advance; publish missing-year coverage, year distribution, and songbook/subgenre confounds; compare piece-level modification rates across composition year while clustering uncertainty by piece and performing a sensitivity analysis excluding records with uncertain dates.
hypotheses.null_model: Year-label permutation within defensible comparison strata; also report the unadjusted relation and missing-data sensitivity.
hypotheses.falsification_or_no_pass: No directional relation after pre-registered sensitivity checks, or too few reliably dated pieces to support the inference.
hypotheses.limitations: Publication date, songbook volume, or style-age stereotypes must not be substituted for a composition year. Do not infer a period from sound alone.
hypotheses.pass_threshold: Pre-register direction, effect and uncertainty rules once metadata coverage is measured.

hypotheses.statement: Historically situated Choro phrase and rhythmic practices may differ among the polca-lundu, tango brasileiro, choro-amaxixado and choro-sambado contexts described by Sève; typical ensembles include string-led and percussion roles but are not universal.
required_additional_evidence: Rights-cleared score, onset or performance annotations with known provenance.
Clear mapping between named historical subtype and each analyzed excerpt.
Review by a knowledgeable Choro practitioner/researcher.
hypotheses.operationalization: Only after source and rights review: measure phrase-level onset/accent patterns and rhythmic asymmetry on a source-defined annotation; compare subtypes and historical periods rather than enforcing one universal template.
hypotheses.null_model: Matched beat-grid/phrase-length baselines that preserve event density; the baseline and subtype labels require expert review before execution.
hypotheses.falsification_or_no_pass: No stable contrast across the registered examples, subtype labels cannot be reliably established, or evidence is insufficient to separate musical pattern from notation/transcription choices.
hypotheses.limitations: The existing chord/form corpus does not alone provide the note-onset and performance-feel evidence required for this test.
hypotheses.pass_threshold: Not specified until a licensed and source-defined rhythm corpus is identified.

sampling_and_dependence.scope_note: The counts below are reported by the cited paper, not recomputed by this repository. The branch has not ingested the corpus. They describe that study's songbook-based sampling frame, not Choro as a whole.
sampling_and_dependence.unit_of_observation: Treat a composition as the minimum indivisible unit for work-level splits; events, bars, chord tokens, parts and phrases from one composition must never be split across train/test partitions.
sampling_and_dependence.primary_split_rule: Any predictive or selection evaluation must split by complete composition before feature extraction or tuning; never randomly split chord tokens, measures or repeated representations from the same piece.
sampling_and_dependence.generalization_sensitivity: Where sample size permits, run a group split that keeps every composition by a composer wholly in one partition. Report composer-held-out performance separately from piece-held-out performance; do not call the former optional evidence of universal authenticity.
dominant_composer_sensitivity: Report results with all eligible works.
Repeat the primary estimate excluding Pixinguinha works.
Repeat the primary estimate excluding Jacob do Bandolim works.
Report whether either exclusion changes effect direction, uncertainty, eligible-work count or qualitative conclusion.
dependence_and_weighting: Report both piece-weighted and composer-aggregated summaries where the question supports both; do not let chord-token volume silently define the sampling weights.

Estimate uncertainty at the highest defensible independent unit for each hypothesis and state that unit explicitly; composer clustering is required for inference intended to generalize across composers.

For historical modification, use composition year only when source provenance supports it; report year missingness and overlap by composer, subgenre and songbook. If period and composer are confounded or have inadequate overlap, report the trend as non-identifiable rather than treating adjustment as a cure.
If too few independent composers or eligible works remain for a planned sensitivity, label it not estimable; do not silently omit the sensitivity.

synthetic_fixture_requirements: Use independently authored small examples; no transcription, melody, chord sequence, or other excerpt copied from the restricted corpus.
Fixture names and annotations describe the tested property, not a claim of authentic Choro.
Prove that the parser/metric responds to a deliberately inserted phrase-position effect and does not respond to a shuffled counterexample.
Pin fixture hashes, algorithm version, random seed, and exact input parameters.
route_promotion_gates: License and source provenance resolved for every evaluation item.
Three primary corpus hypotheses registered before empirical analysis; separate eligibility/coverage report published.
Results reproduce under a held-out-by-composition split and constrained nulls.
Neighboring-style distinctness test uses independent, compatible and rights-cleared reference material.
A knowledgeable Choro musician/researcher reviews the proposed grammar and limitations.
An actual executable composer path is added and tested through the same call path used by users.
Renderer/instrument availability and every substitution are reported separately from symbolic grammar results.
No cultural authenticity or faithful-generation claim until the applicable review and evidence gates pass.

future_receipt_required: exact preregistered analysis-plan file SHA-256 and immutable registration URL
exact plan-to-manifest source binding comparison for source IDs, artifact URLs/paths/digests/bytes and selected work IDs
registered primary hypotheses, concrete null models, threshold/uncertainty rules, multiplicity policy, missing-data policy, split strategy and mandatory sensitivity analyses

checks: phrase-position metric distinguishes authored aligned fixture from a counterexample and balanced phase rotation null
conditional transition entropy distinguishes a deterministic authored cycle from a seeded shuffle while preserving symbol counts
trend metric detects a monotone synthetic series and its reversed counterexample
invalid or degenerate input fails closed
limits: synthetic fixtures do not validate Choro-specific claims
no third-party corpus data or musical excerpts are used
commercial corpus use still requires appropriate rights clearance

alternative_source_intake.note: Per-work source leads only. No score data is copied or analyzed; commercial or empirical use remains gated on an appropriate rights review.

preregistration.title: Welcome to Registrations & Preregistrations
supports: plan timestamped and read-only before collection or analysis
explicit hypotheses and variables, statistical tests, decision criteria, exclusions, outcomes, contingencies, and planned deviations
preregistration.limitation: This repository validates recorded plan fields and a supplied HTTPS URL; it does not independently verify that an external registration exists or that its contents are immutable.

music_generation_evaluation.title: Recent advances in music generation: methods, evaluation, and challenges
supports: no single objective metric covers every relevant aspect of generated music
symbolic and audio evaluation emphasize different outcome families, including tonality/rhythm/structure versus timbre/transients/perceptual quality
design_implications: report multiple registered metrics with distinct interpretations
separate source-corpus evidence from runtime response, rendered-audio evidence, and expert/listener evaluation
